messages:
samir: Heads-up — we're planning a mid-April rollout of the new GPU inference fleet in eu-west-1 behind NLBs and private VPC endpoints. We need to pre-emptively raise a few soft limits: target registration rate for NLB target groups, per-VPCE target count (interface endpoints), and possibly ENI/prefix limits for the account. This will be ~1200 targets registering across 6 AZs over a short window. Can ops advise the exact numbers to request and the recommended AWS case wording? :wave:

alex_chang: +1. What are the concrete numbers you expect per AZ and the registration burst profile? AWS cares about both the per-second registration rate and the per-target-group capacity.

samir: Rough breakdown: 1200 total targets (roughly 200 per AZ). We expect registration to happen in ~10 minutes during scale events -> ~200/sec peak registration across AZs (clients will stagger but want headroom). For VPCEs: 150 interface endpoints (mostly private-ips for internal inference), current soft limit is 50 in eu-west-1 IIRC. ENI/prefixes: each GPU host will create extra ENIs for plugins, expecting ~2k additional ENIs.

tara: Ok. For the quota requests I'd ask for: NLB target registration rate -> 500/sec, target group target limit -> 3k, VPCE interface endpoints -> 200, and ENI limit -> +2500. Use the AWS Service Quotas console and also open a Support ticket with Business-critical justification (we're launching a customer-facing real-time inference product). Give examples of traffic patterns and a rollout timeline.

maria: Also verify subnet IP capacity. If we attach many ENIs in a single subnet you can run out of private IPs even with quota bumps. Recommend adding /22s or adding additional subnets per AZ.

kevin: Suggestion: avoid a single coherent registration spike — can we do a registration ramp with 5% increments and 5-min pauses? That reduces the chance we hit per-second throttles. Also consider pre-warming targets: register a small number of targets in each group ahead of time and then roll in the rest.

samir: Good call. We still want official quota increases as fallback. Can someone draft the Support case text? I'll paste the specifics and timeline.

alex_chang: Draft below — copy into Support Center and Service Quotas request. Tailor numbers if infra pushes back.

``` 
Subject: Urgent quota increase request — NLB target registration rate, target count, VPCEs, ENIs (eu-west-1)

Account: redwood-prod (account-id: 123456789012)
Region: eu-west-1

Request:
- Increase NLB target registration rate to 500 registrations/second (current default causes throttling during fleet rollouts).
- Increase per-target-group target limit to 3,000 targets.
- Increase EC2 Network Interface (ENI) quota by +2,500.
- Increase number of Interface VPC Endpoints (VPCE) in eu-west-1 to 200.

Justification:
We are launching a GPU inference fleet that will register ~1,200 backend targets distributed across 6 AZs during scale events. The service powers real-time customer traffic (low latency SLOs) and requires predictable registration throughput to avoid cold-start failures. We already stagger registrations in our rollout plan but require quota increases to ensure headroom and to support planned growth. Timeline: planned rollout start 2026-04-17, with incremental scaling over two weeks.

Contact: Samir (Infra), alex_chang (Ops)

Please escalate to the Elastic Load Balancing and EC2 service teams for review.
```

samir: This looks solid. One extra note: call out that many of the endpoints are private (VPCE) used by dedicated customer workloads and will be created under our Private deployment. Add that to the justification.

alex_chang: Updated draft — add the VPCE bit and the subnet/IP risk Maria mentioned. Also attach our rollout plan (s3 link) and a short CSV of expected targets per AZ.

samir: I'll paste the rollout S3 link in the ticket and the CSV. Can someone run the Service Quotas request too?

quota-bot: Service Quotas request submitted by alex_chang. Request IDs: SQ-NE-2026-000123 (NLB target registration rate), SQ-NE-2026-000124 (target count), SQ-NE-2026-000125 (ENI), SQ-NE-2026-000126 (VPCE).

ops-bot: Support case opened: case-id 9876543210. AWS SE assigned. Expected initial response 24-48 hrs. Tags: inference-gpu-fleet, eu-west-1, priority-high. :thumbsup:

maria: Until quotas are confirmed, please avoid creating a full-scale registration job. Run a smoke with 5% of target volume and verify target health checks + connection churn. Also run `aws ec2 describe-managed-prefix-lists` and validate IP availability in subnets used.

kevin: I'll help implement the ramp script and can add a circuit-breaker for failed registrations. We should also keep a fallback to an older model pool in case some AZs hit limits.

samir: Thanks all. I'll paste the final Support case when AWS replies. For now: alex_chang — can you track the quota request IDs and drop updates here? Will coordinate the smoke window once quotas look green. :pray:
